title: Links, images and lists
lesson:
**Lists:** `
    ` is a bulleted list, `
      ` a numbered one; each item is an `
    1. `. **Links:** `Kiwix`. The `href` **attribute** says where it goes; the text between the tags is what people click. Links to other pages in your own folder are just the file name: `Crops`. Write link text that makes sense on its own ("the planting calendar", not "click here"): people using screen readers often jump from link to link. **Images:** ``. `img` has no closing tag. `src` is the file; `alt` describes the picture for people who can't see it, for screen readers, and for when the image fails to load on a slow connection. Every image needs `alt`; a purely decorative one gets `alt=""`. **Attributes** go inside the opening tag as `name="value"`. You've now seen `lang`, `charset`, `href`, `src` and `alt`; `id` and `class` (names for styling and scripts) come next.

example.code:
Our crops

  • Maize
  • Beans
  • Sukuma wiki
  1. Prepare the soil
  2. Plant after the first rains

Read more on Appropedia.

quiz.q: Why does every image need alt text?
choices: For people who can't see it, screen readers, and slow connections where it doesn't load
